body:
(Replaces my notes of 10:51 and 10:43 UTC. Corrected again after reading app/lib/data/encore/encore_mutations.dart: on an ENCORE server the playlist edits do not go through playlist_mutations.dart, which is the old music-server mode.)

WHERE: `applyPlaylists` (app/lib/data/encore/encore_writer.dart:153-215) writes the server's name, cover and `deletedAtMs: null` for every playlist row of the feed, replaces the entries it brings and calls `_renumber`. The existing protection, `pendingStarTargets` (data/sync/pending_intent.dart:13), looks only at outbox kinds `star`/`unstar`.

THE KINDS THAT WAIT (encore_mutations.dart:10-27): `e.playlist.create` {id, name, entries[{ref,id}]}, `e.playlist.add` {playlistId, entries[{ref,id}]}, `e.playlist.remove` {playlistId, entryIds[pe_...]}, `e.playlist.rename` {playlistId, name}, `e.playlist.delete` {id}. Every id is the phone's own (`pl_`, `pe_`), and a local entry row already carries its `pe_` id and a local `serverPosition` (encore_mutations.dart:72-80, 113-121).

WHAT THE SERVER DOES (library.py): a delivered rename or delete touches the PLAYLIST in the change log (lines 138-158), and `changes()` (363-405) returns the playlist row whole; so for name, cover and delete, skipping while the edit waits is safe, the delivery brings the playlist back. Entries are returned one TOUCHED entry at a time, each with its own older sequence number, so skipping a whole playlist during a pull would lose another device's entry for good. Protect per field:
 1. Name: skip the write while an `e.playlist.rename` for that playlist waits. A playlist deleted on the server still wins over a waiting rename (docs/34 CF-21): keep the tombstone branch.
 2. A waiting delete: skip `deletedAtMs: null` while an `e.playlist.delete` for it waits (otherwise the deleted playlist comes back until it is delivered).
 3. Waiting removals: do not re-insert an entry whose own `pe_` id is in a waiting `e.playlist.remove`. Exact, by entry id; no matching by track.
 4. A waiting ADD is safe on an Encore server: the local row has a `pe_` id, `_renumber` (225-232) deletes only rows with NO entry id (the old mode), and the delivered entry comes back with the same id. Do not add a protection for it. Check one thing in the test: `_renumber` sorts by `serverPosition`, and a waiting local add has the phone's own value (`i + 1.0`) on the server's scale, so it may sit in the wrong place until delivery.
 A parked (failed) edit stops protecting, as for likes (pending_intent.dart:5-8).

No new app call is needed. The arbiter is an end-to-end test: a rename waits, the feed brings the old name and another device's added song: the screen keeps the new name AND shows the song; after delivery both. A removal waits, the feed brings the entry: it stays gone. A delete waits, the feed brings the playlist: it stays deleted.

TESTS: test/data/encore/encore_sync_test.dart:214 is the likes test (outbox insert at 221 is the pattern). Docs: docs/34 rule 5 (line 17) says "a like or unlike": widen it and its test column.
